title: Baby, Come to Me
year_note: On Every Home Should Have One (September 1981); the single came out in April 1982 and reached number one in February 1983.

notes.made: Rod Temperton wrote and arranged it and Quincy Jones produced, at Westlake in Los Angeles and Mediasound in New York between March and May 1981, with Bruce Swedien recording and mixing. John Robinson plays drums, Steve Lukather guitar, Greg Phillinganes keyboards, Richard Tee Fender Rhodes, and David Foster is among the synth players. Michael McDonald sings backing vocals.
notes.context: Austin was Jones's goddaughter and the first artist he signed to Qwest. The single stalled at 73 in May 1982. Then ABC's General Hospital started playing it as the love theme for Luke Spencer, viewers called in, and Warner Bros. reissued it in October. It reached number one on 19 February 1983, stayed two weeks and spent seven months on the Hot 100.

listen_for.note: Michael McDonald is in the backing vocals, under Ingram and Austin.
Richard Tee's Rhodes, the same player as on Just the Two of Us.

leads_to.title: One Hundred Ways
leads_to.why: Ingram's lead vocal on Jones's The Dude, the same year, which won him the Best Male R&B Vocal Grammy.

culture.title: General Hospital
culture.line: In 1982 ABC's General Hospital used it as the love theme for Luke Spencer, and so many viewers asked about it that Warner Bros. reissued the single that October.

culture.title: From 73 to number one
culture.line: First time out it peaked at 73 on 8 May 1982. The reissue reached number one on 19 February 1983 for two weeks, topped adult contemporary and got to 11 in the UK.

culture.title: Covers
culture.line: Shirley Bassey, Dalida, Alexander O'Neal and Cherrelle, and Daryl Hall with Kenny G have all recorded it.
